issues.description: Card number stored in database without encryption or tokenization. Storing raw card data violates PCI-DSS compliance standards and exposes sensitive payment information.
issues.suggestion: Never store raw card numbers. Use a payment processor's tokenization service (Stripe, Square, PayPal) that returns a token instead of the actual card number. Store only the token and last 4 digits.

issues.description: PaymentDetails interface stores sensitive card data (cardNumber, CVV, expiryDate) in memory. This data should never be stored in the application, only transmitted to payment processors.
issues.suggestion: Remove cardNumber, CVV, and expiryDate from this interface. Accept only a tokenized payment method identifier from a PCI-compliant payment processor.

issues.description: Payment validation logic is not PCI-DSS compliant. Card validation should happen on client-side or through a tokenization service, not server-side handling of raw card data.
issues.suggestion: Use a payment processor's client-side library (Stripe.js, etc.) to handle card validation and tokenization before sending to backend. Backend should never receive raw card data.

issues.description: Syntax error: rows[0]] has an extra closing bracket. This will cause a runtime error when the function tries to access subscription data.
issues.suggestion: Fix the syntax error: change 'const subscription = rows[0]];' to 'const subscription = rows[0];'

issues.description: Card expiry date validation has a Y2K-like bug. Using '2000 + parseInt(year)' assumes all cards are from 2000-2099, but cards can have valid expiry years up to 2099 in YY format, creating incorrect validation.
issues.suggestion: Use proper date parsing with century context awareness. For YY format, years 00-30 should be 2000-2030, and 31-99 should be 1931-1999, or accept MM/YYYY format instead.

issues.description: Card number validation is insufficient. Only checks length, but doesn't validate Luhn algorithm, which is the industry standard for card validation.
issues.suggestion: Implement Luhn algorithm validation for card numbers. Libraries like 'credit-card-type' or 'luhn' can help, but again - this should be on client-side only.

issues.description: No idempotency handling for payment processing. If the function fails after chargeCard succeeds but before upgradeUserSubscription completes, the payment is charged but subscription not updated.
issues.suggestion: Implement idempotency keys and wrap payment processing in a transaction. Use a database transaction that ensures both payment recording and subscription upgrade succeed together.

issues.description: No logging of payment attempts for audit trail. Payment transactions must be logged for compliance, dispute resolution, and fraud detection.
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive logging of all payment attempts, including userId, amount, status, timestamp, and any errors. Ensure logs are stored securely and separately from transaction data.

issues.description: N+1 query pattern risk. Every call to hasFeatureAccess queries the database individually. If checking multiple features for multiple users, this causes excessive queries.
issues.suggestion: Add caching layer (Redis) with appropriate TTL to cache subscription data. Consider batch loading subscriptions when checking multiple users or features.

issues.description: JSON.parse without try-catch on line 131 and 146. If stored features JSON is corrupted, this will throw an uncaught error and crash the application.
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch blocks with appropriate error handling and logging. Use a schema validation library like Zod to validate parsed JSON structure.

issues.description: Tax and processing fee calculations are hardcoded. These are configuration values that should be externalized for easy updates without code deployment.
issues.suggestion: Move TAX_RATE and PROCESSING_FEE to environment variables or configuration database. Consider implementing a pricing service.

issues.description: Error handling in chargeCard only logs and returns false. No distinction between different error types (network error, invalid amount, card declined, etc.).
issues.suggestion: Implement proper error handling with specific error types. Return or throw structured errors containing error codes, retry information, and user-friendly messages.

issues.description: No validation of userId format. Accepts any string, which could allow NoSQL injection or database manipulation through crafted userIds.
issues.suggestion: Add validation for userId to ensure it matches expected format (UUID, numeric ID, etc.). Use a validation library like Zod for type-safe runtime validation.

issues.description: Features array is hardcoded in the function. If adding new features, this requires code changes and redeployment.
issues.suggestion: Move feature sets to a configuration or database table. Implement a feature flags system to manage feature access across tiers.

issues.description: Magic number 1 year for subscription validity. Not configurable and not clearly explained why 1 year was chosen.
issues.suggestion: Extract subscription duration to a constant or configuration. Add comments explaining the business logic.

issues.description: Generic error message 'Invalid payment details' doesn't indicate which field is invalid, making debugging difficult.
issues.suggestion: Return specific validation errors indicating which field failed validation and why (e.g., 'Invalid card number length' instead of generic message).

issues.description: SQL query string is long and hard to read. Could benefit from formatting for better maintainability.
issues.suggestion: Consider using a query builder or template literals to make SQL queries more readable and maintainable.

codeQuality.summary: This payment processing code has critical security vulnerabilities related to handling raw credit card data, which violates PCI-DSS compliance standards. The most urgent issues are: (1) storing unencrypted card numbers in the database, (2) accepting and processing raw card data server-side instead of using tokenization, (3) a critical syntax error that will cause runtime failures. Additionally, there are significant issues with transaction integrity (payment charged but subscription not updated), insufficient error handling, lack of audit logging, and no caching strategy leading to potential N+1 query problems. The code lacks comprehensive test coverage. Recommendation: Completely refactor to use a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, Square, PayPal) that handles tokenization client-side, implement database transactions, add comprehensive error handling and logging, and add full test coverage before production deployment.

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL: This payment processing module has 0% test coverage with 33 distinct untested paths. All 6 exported/key functions are completely untested. This includes critical paths for payment validation, card charging, subscription upgrades, and access control. 15 paths are marked critical priority due to direct financial/security impact. The module requires comprehensive unit tests covering: (1) Payment flow end-to-end with mocked database and chargeCard function, (2) Validation logic edge cases for all card details, (3) Pricing calculations for both tiers, (4) Date/expiry handling boundary cases, (5) Error scenarios and graceful degradation, (6) Feature access control logic with expired/active subscriptions, (7) Subscription CRUD operations. Without these tests, this code is unsuitable for production use. Estimated minimum: 40+ test cases needed for adequate coverage.

refactorings.summary: The premium.ts file has significant refactoring opportunities focusing on separation of concerns, code reuse, and design patterns. Key recommendations: (1) Extract pricing logic into Strategy pattern for tier flexibility, (2) Centralize feature and tier definitions to reduce duplication, (3) Break down card validation into composable functions, (4) Implement payment processing pipeline pattern for better testability, (5) Create helper functions for common operations, (6) Consolidate SQL queries, (7) Use branded types for subscription tiers. These changes would improve maintainability, testability, and reduce cognitive load. The highest-impact improvements are the Strategy pattern for pricing, Pipeline pattern for payment processing, and centralization of configuration and queries.

recommendations.description: Immediately refactor to use a PCI-DSS compliant payment processor (Stripe, Square, PayPal). The application should never handle, store, or process raw credit card data. Replace PaymentDetails interface to accept only tokenized payment method identifiers.
Fix syntax error on line 127: change 'const subscription = rows[0]];' to 'const subscription = rows[0];'. This will cause runtime failures when accessing subscription data.

Implement comprehensive test coverage (minimum 40+ test cases) for all payment-related functions. Currently at 0% test coverage for a critical financial module. Cover payment flows, validation, pricing, and feature access control.

Implement database transactions and idempotency keys to ensure payment charging and subscription upgrade are atomic operations. Prevent situations where payment succeeds but subscription update fails.
Add comprehensive logging of all payment attempts, including userId, amount, status, timestamp, and error details. This is required for compliance, dispute resolution, and fraud detection.

Implement structured error handling with specific error types for different failure scenarios (network error, invalid amount, card declined, etc.). Replace generic error messages with context-specific feedback.
Add runtime validation for userId and payment parameters using a library like Zod. Implement Luhn algorithm for card number validation and numeric-only checks for CVV.
Implement caching layer (Redis) for subscription data to prevent N+1 query patterns. Add batch loading capability for checking multiple users or features.

Extract hardcoded configurations (pricing tiers, tax rates, processing fees, feature sets) into environment variables or configuration database. Externalize subscription duration and other business logic constants.

Apply Strategy pattern to pricing logic, Pipeline pattern to payment processing, and extract database queries into centralized constants. These changes will significantly improve testability and maintainability.
